messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: increased DNS resolver failures observed from edge probes in eu-west-1. error: SERVFAIL from primary external resolvers (provider A). Automatic failover not triggered yet. Initial spike at 11:12 UTC. Paging oncall @Oncall-SRE

Maria G: Ack, looking. I see health checks for our geo-dns control plane showing elevated latency to provider A's API.

TJ: Any user-facing errors? support-bot do we have tickets?

Support Bot: 23 new tickets created in the last 10m showing failures to resolve hostname for hosted endpoints (500s coming from origin due to client-layer DNS timeouts). Top regions: EU (IE, FR), UK.

Eli: Running digs from eu-probe-1: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> A api.customer1.redwood.ai @8.8.8.8
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, id: 12345
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 0, AUTHORITY: 1, ADDITIONAL: 1
```

Maria G: I'm also seeing repeated 504s in the LB logs where backend TLS succeeded but client couldn't resolve the CNAME. Likely resolver upstream returning SERVFAIL causing our SDK fallback to not hit cache.

opsbot: Noted. Provider-A status page: https://status.provider-a.example.com/incidents/abc123 (reports "degraded DNS resolution in EU")

Oncall-SRE: Thanks. Quick triage: 1) Is this impacting all customers or a subset pinned to provider-A? 2) Can we trigger immediate GeoDNS weight flip to secondary provider B for eu-west-1? 3) Short TTLs/flush caches to accelerate failover if we flip.

Sam K: For question 1 — we onboarded a small subset of customers (BYO DNS -> provider A) last quarter. But our default hosted customers use GeoDNS and two upstreams (A,B) with weights skewed to A for latency; seems like those fallback rules aren't switching due to provider A returning SERVFAIL rather than connection error.

TJ: Ok. If we flip weights in the control plane we need to also lower TTL to 30s and then roll back after. Who can run the change? Maria?

Maria G: I can run the control plane update. Proposed steps: 
1) patch geo-config to set eu-west priority: provider-B 100, provider-A 0 
2) lower zone TTL for affected records to 30s (via our DNS provider API) 
3) purge CDN resolver caches for the last-hop caches we control 
4) monitor resolver probe success and customer ticket rate

Oncall-SRE: Sounds good. Add a temporary route: update health-check policy to prefer local caches first to avoid hitting problematic resolvers while propagation occurs. Also add a fallback rule: if provider-A returns SERVFAIL, treat as failure and fall back immediately (we currently only treat timeouts as failures).

Maria G: Implementing now. Command I'm running: ```bash
# flip geodns weights
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer ${INTERNAL_API_KEY}" 
  https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/geodns/set-weights 
  -d '{"region":"eu-west-1","weights":{"provider-B":100,"provider-A":0}}'
# lower TTL
curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/dns/set-ttl -d '{"zone":"redwood.ai","ttl":30}'
```
(Will paste response in a sec)

opsbot: Change accepted. Job id: job-8923. Rolling.

Maria G: Geo config response: 200 OK. TTL change: 202 Accepted (propagation to provider pending). Pushing cache purge to CDN edge: ``curl -X POST https://internal-api.redwood.ai/v1/cdn/purge -d '{"pattern":"*.redwood.ai"}'`` -> accepted job-8924.

Eli: Running probes again from eu-probe-1: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> A api.customer1.redwood.ai @1.1.1.1
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: NOERROR, id: 67890
;; flags: qr rd ra; QUERY: 1, ANSWER: 1
api.customer1.redwood.ai. 30 IN A 3.3.3.3
```
Looks like provider-B returning answers now.

Support Bot: New tickets reduced to 6 in the last 10m. Error rate for EU region is down 75% (was 12% of requests, now 3%).

Product Ops: Heads up — a couple of enterprise customers were affected (contracted SLAs). We're drafting a short incident update. Can you capture start times and affected customers?

TJ: I'll take post-incident analysis. For now we need on-call continuity. Maria you ran the mitigation — could you hand off to me for monitoring and followups?

Maria G: Handing off to @TJ — elevated TTLs were lowered and weights flipped; caches purged. Estimated full global propagation in ~90s. Logs show recovery starting at 11:15 UTC. 

TJ: Taking the incident. :rotating_light: I'll stay on for the next 2h to monitor and prepare RCA. Oncall-SRE, please keep an eye on provider-A's status and whether additional mitigations (rate limiting provider-A, removing as upstream entirely) are needed.

Oncall-SRE: Acknowledged. Next steps: 1) Keep geo-weights as-is for 30m; 2) If provider-A still reports degraded after 30m, schedule planned removal from pool and notify sales/CS for impacted customers; 3) Add rule in our control plane to treat SERVFAIL as failure for geo-failover decisions (postmortem item).

opsbot: Incident severity set to SEV2. Created incident ticket INC-2024-074. Notifying #oncall-handoff.

Support Bot: Creating a consolidated response template for support with steps customers can take (clear local DNS, switch to provider-B/8.8.8.8) — will link in incident doc.

Maria G: Leaving monitoring to TJ. I'm dropping from the thread to wrap up the rollout change logs. Good catch everyone. :thumbsup:

TJ: A few quick notes for handoff: 
- start: 1747654321 (11:12 UTC)
- mitigation applied: 1747654350 (11:15 UTC) - geo weights flipped + TTL lowered + CDN purge
- initial ticket spike: ~23 open, now 6 ongoing
- affected regions: eu-west-1 primarily (IE, FR, UK)
- suspected root cause: provider-A returning SERVFAIL under partial outage causing our geo-failover logic to not treat as upstream failure

TJ: I'll update INC-2024-074 with these, collect probe logs, and schedule a postmortem with SRE and Product Ops tomorrow. If anyone sees reblips ping me directly.

incident-bot: NOTE: This thread will be archived when incident is closed.
